items.purpose: Exploded isometric schematic of the Chandrayaan-3 composite: Propulsion Module, Vikram Lander, Pragyan Rover (Slide 02)
items.prompt: Technical blueprint schematic style. Clean precise lines on an implied subtle grid, with deliberate geometric rigor — right angles, parallel rules, measured spacing. Elements are simplified to essential schematic forms — boxes, cylinders, connector lines, anchor dots, callout markers with no text. Color is restrained and near-monochrome with one semantic accent. A very-low-opacity grid background at about 6% reinforces the schematic feel. No textures, no shading, no painterly artifacts. Overall feel is engineering-precise, analytical, intentional, as in a spacecraft assembly drawing hung on a wall. Deck color behavior: the deep navy background #0B1A2B is the blueprint paper and fills the whole field; the light blue primary #8AB4E8 carries every schematic line, edge, frame and dimension rule at a crisp uniform 1.5px stroke with no fills; the darker secondary accent #4E7FA8 carries only the faint 6% grid and the receding hidden edges; the orange accent #FF7A3D appears on strictly one element — the smallest body at the bottom of the stack — and on nothing else. Composition: an exploded isometric stack in true 30 degree axonometric projection, three separated bodies aligned on one shared vertical assembly axis drawn as a thin long-dash centre line running top to bottom through all three. Top body: a squat hexagonal-prism propulsion module with a cylindrical propellant tank suggested inside by hidden dashed edges, a flat circular thruster ring on its underside, and two rectangular solar panels extended on opposite sides as thin outlined planes with an internal line lattice of parallel cell divisions. Middle body: a box-shaped lander with slightly tapered sides, four straight landing legs splayed outward ending in small round footpads, four downward-pointing thruster nozzles drawn as small truncated cones on its base, a small flat antenna disc on its upper deck, and a short ramp element folded against one flank. Bottom body: a small six-wheeled rover, low and rectangular, its six wheels drawn as thin outlined cylinders on two rocker-bogie arms, one flat solar panel raised above its deck, and a tiny mast — this rover is the single element drawn in orange accent #FF7A3D. Thin leader lines with small open arrowheads reach outward from each of the three bodies toward the empty margins and simply stop, leaving clear empty space at the ends of every leader so editable labels can be placed beside them later. Small square anchor ticks mark each leader origin. Two vertical dimension brackets with fine end serifs run down the left side spanning the separation gaps between bodies. Composed as a 1024x768 local schematic block with generous inner padding of about 12%, the stack occupying the centre and the outer margins left calm and empty for overlay labels. NO text of any kind anywhere in the image — no letters, numbers, signs, watermarks, labels, or written symbols. Color values (HEX codes like #8AB4E8) and color names are rendering guidance only — do NOT display HEX codes, color names, or palette labels as visible text anywhere in the image.

items.purpose: Schematic map band of the lunar south polar region with the landing ellipse highlighted (Slide 06)
items.prompt: Technical blueprint schematic style. Clean precise lines on an implied subtle grid, with deliberate geometric rigor — concentric rules, parallel graticule lines, measured spacing. Terrain is reduced to essential schematic forms — outlined crater rings, contour rings, hairline graticule, anchor dots, callout markers. Color is restrained and near-monochrome with one semantic accent. A very-low-opacity grid at about 6% reinforces the schematic feel. No textures, no shading, no photographic detail, no painterly artifacts. Overall feel is engineering-precise, analytical and cartographic, like a polar landing-site chart on drafting paper. Deck color behavior: the deep navy background #0B1A2B is the paper and fills the whole field; the light blue primary #8AB4E8 carries every crater outline, contour ring, graticule line and dimension rule as a crisp uniform 1 to 1.5px stroke with no fills; the darker secondary accent #4E7FA8 carries the faintest background graticule and the smallest secondary craters; the orange accent #FF7A3D marks exactly one thing — a small rectangular target box near the centre-left with a fine crosshair inside it — and nothing else. Composition: a wide polar chart seen straight down. A hairline polar graticule of concentric circles and radial spokes spans the whole band, densest near the centre. Scattered across it, roughly thirty overlapping crater outlines of widely varying diameter, each drawn as a simple circle or slightly irregular closed outline with a second inner rim circle and a few short radial ejecta ticks outside the larger ones; several large degraded basins are suggested only by long shallow arcs that run off the edges of the frame. Two or three broad smooth plateau regions are indicated by nested contour rings with no fill. The small orange target box with its crosshair sits inside a relatively smooth area between two large crater rims, and one thin orange leader line runs from it toward the lower right and stops in empty space. A fine horizontal scale bar with tick marks and no numbers sits in the lower left corner; a small north-arrow triangle with a thin circle around it sits in the upper right corner. The lower third of the right half is deliberately left as calm empty paper with only the faintest graticule, reserved for an editable overlay. Composed as a 1920x1080 wide local band, terrain filling the frame edge to edge with no vignette. NO text of any kind anywhere in the image — no letters, numbers, signs, coordinates, watermarks, labels, or written symbols. items.purpose: Cross-section figure of lunar regolith layering with a depth scale, for the ChaSTE and hop-experiment page (Slide 10)
items.prompt: Technical blueprint schematic style. Clean precise lines on an implied subtle grid, with deliberate geometric rigor — right angles, parallel rules, measured spacing and true drafting conventions. Forms are reduced to essential schematic elements — section hatching, boundary rules, dimension lines with end serifs, anchor dots. Color is restrained and near-monochrome with one semantic accent. A very-low-opacity grid at about 6% reinforces the schematic feel. No textures, no shading, no painterly artifacts. Overall feel is engineering-precise and analytical, like a soil-mechanics section drawing. Deck color behavior: the deep navy background #0B1A2B is the paper; the light blue primary #8AB4E8 carries every boundary line, hatch stroke, dimension rule and probe outline at a crisp uniform 1 to 1.5px stroke with no solid fills; the darker secondary accent #4E7FA8 carries the faint grid and the sparsest hatching of the deepest zone; the orange accent #FF7A3D marks exactly one element — the slender temperature probe driven into the section — and nothing else. Composition: a vertical section through the top of a granular surface, seen edge on, filling the frame. A straight horizontal surface line runs across the upper third. Below it the section is divided into three stacked zones separated by two horizontal boundary rules: a very thin top zone drawn with widely spaced fine dots and small open circles to read as loose hyper-porous dust; a middle zone with sparse diagonal hatching at 45 degrees and a few small outlined grains; a deeper zone with dense diagonal hatching in the opposite direction and larger outlined angular grains, reading as compacted material. On the left edge a vertical dimension line with fine end serifs and evenly spaced tick marks forms a depth scale; the ticks are labelled with the numerals 0, 3 and 6.5 set in a small clean fixed-width technical typeface, plus the two lowercase letters cm placed once at the top of that scale, and nothing else is written anywhere. On the right, a slender orange probe with a pointed tip and a small square head penetrates vertically from the surface line down into the middle zone, with five tiny square sensor ticks along its shaft; one thin orange leader line runs from the probe head out to the right margin and stops in empty space. Above the surface line on the right, a faint cone of short radiating hairlines suggests exhaust sweeping the surface, and two very short arrows show fine particles lifting away. The upper left corner is left as calm empty paper for an editable overlay. Composed as a 1024x768 local figure block with about 10% inner padding. Apart from the numerals 0, 3, 6.5 and the two letters cm on the depth scale, NO other text, labels, watermarks or written symbols appear anywhere in the image. Color values (HEX codes like #8AB4E8) and color names are rendering guidance only — do NOT display HEX codes, color names, or palette labels as visible text anywhere in the image.
